SBP: Give orders to units to begin responding to the scene and assessing the situation.
Establish roles amongst members according to the ICS (Incident Commander, Supporting Roles)
Designate triage, treatment, transport, staging, casualty collection/morgue areas

Take into consideration the importance to not overburden hospitals – sending all the critical patients to one hospital, remembering the number of walking wounded that will potentially go to these hospitals and the number of patients they may already have.
Decide on the map area to lead people away from the building safely, where to gather.
Firefighters must go in first and ensure scene safety – no active fires, structural safety.

Consider that this detonation may be a terrorist attack – does it include biowarfare agents? Nuclear radiation? Could there be a second attack once first responders enter? Or a second, larger attack on the street?

Learns should consider coordinating with police, homeland security and other potential law enforcement agencies about ensuring scene safety outside the building and closing down streets to use as space for patients.
Participants should have some individuals designated to retrieve patients, others to triage and others to treat.
Direct them to staging area for assignments.
